items.title: Howard Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: So when Cecil Bridgewater came in to do that last big band record of Dee Dee Bridgewater, Jim Anderson came over

ctx.x: The great engineer Jim Anderson, who did a lot of wonderful recordings for us all, asked somebody when he was doing a big band, asked somebody why are there not any black players in the band. And the guy very openly told him what I just said, you know. Not reliable with the pitch and yada-yada-yada. So when Cecil Bridgewater came in to do that last big band record of Dee Dee Bridgewater, Jim Anderson came over and said, “Are these guys from the West Coast?” He said, “No they’re in New York.” Jim said, “Well

they’re excellent players.” Cecil went, “Well thank you.” He went, “But they’re all black.” And told Cecil what people had been telling him. Cecil first looked around the room and went, “Oh, you’re right.” Because it’s no big thing. You know it just turned out that way. There wasn’t anything like, “Don’t get any white guys.” So where does any of that stand? It’s impossible to know or at least hard to know.
